blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Finetuning Beats LoRA: A Gentle Intro to Preserving Knowledge in Foundation Models
blogs.description: Dive into the core idea behind Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): keeping the pair‑wise angles between neurons intact during adaptation. We’ll explain why orthogonal transforms naturally preserve spectral norms, how this leads to more stable training, and compare with the popular low‑rank LoRA approach. No math heavy – just intuitive analogies and real‑world benefits.

blogs.title: From Block‑Diagonal to Butterfly: How BOFT Makes Huge Transformers Smarter with Fewer Parameters
blogs.description: Unpack the leap from OFT’s block‑diagonal structure to Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT). Using a network‑topology analogy, we’ll show how butterfly matrices squeeze a dense orthogonal matrix into a handful of sparse factors, cutting trainable parameters from quadratic to nearly linear. Readers will see real numbers from experimental results and understand why this matters for large vision and language models.

blogs.title: Information Transmission View: Turning Matrix Factorization Into a Graph Problem
blogs.description: Explore the novel perspective that views orthogonal matrix construction as transmitting data on a grid graph. We’ll walk through simple examples (e.g., 4×4 matrices) and illustrate how butterfly “butterfly” patterns achieve dense connectivity with minimal edges. The post will demystify why sparse factorization can still yield powerful, expressive transforms.

blogs.title: Butterfly Matrices Around the Internet: From Fast Fourier Transform to Model Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: Give readers an accessible history of butterfly structures in signal processing (FFT) and networking, then link that heritage to BOFT’s application in fine‑tuning foundation models. Highlight key insights such as implicit inductive bias, structured generalization, and how classic transforms like Hadamard and DCT emerge naturally within BOFT’s parameter space.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: Implementing BOFT on Your Favorite Vision or Language Model
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step recipe for hobbyists and researchers looking to try BOFT. Cover library support, hyperparameter choices (block size vs number of layers), initialization tricks (identity vs Cayley), and tricks like multiplicative dropout. End with concrete code snippets (PyTorch/TensorFlow) and performance benchmarks on common downstream tasks.
